steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It's not getting through.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Who are you calling, Saria?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Tin Man.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: The metal guy? Did something happen?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: I'm afraid so. Maylander would not have joined our pursuers otherwise.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The army has an agreement with Maylander? Why are they targeting us? What happened to the Tin Man?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I had a look around the way you taught me, Saria. All the soldiers are gone, and so are the agents who were on us.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The pursuers would not have disappeared if she was just staying as the rear guard.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Unless—she offered something that satisfied them.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: The silver liquid? I saw it around her!

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...Transmitter?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She was in contact with Dorothy at Site 359 and undoubtedly got the Transmitter from her. Does Dorothy expect her to do something?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Dorothy is still in military custody. She couldn't possibly be trying to reach out to the military and Ferdinand through her.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Could it be Parvis or...?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Saria...

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Don't worry, Ifrit.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She'll be fine.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I'm trying to tell you not to squeeze your communicator so hard. You're crushing it.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: ...Thanks.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: I'm not worried. Silence isn't so reckless.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: She stayed after she talked to you. I'm sure she thought it through.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: She doesn't know what she's up against. The machinations of the state are far crueler than she can imagine.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: You think she doesn't know that? I'm sure she thought about it.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Silence works hard. She's always working when I see her. The others say it's like she's being chased by something you can't see or touch.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Maybe this'll all be cleared up by the time we see her again.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Then I'll tell her, yeah, I'm upset you left me behind, but I knew you could do it.
Saria notices that Ifrit's hands are trembling. She wants to say something to comfort her.
But words fail her.
She realizes that, even though Ifrit's words were, in part, intended to comfort, she does not know the Silence that Ifrit speaks of.
Silence is ready. Silence knows what she is about to face.
She has never thought about it that way.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Over there, Saria.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: The army is pulling out, but not in direction of the military garrison.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Is the Transmitter really the clue to Kristen's whereabouts?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Let's follow them.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Silence wouldn't want you to put yourself in danger again.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: She promised we would go together!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: She said, 'Saria will return here the moment she wakes up.' 'That's the sort of woman she is.'

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: It's not...

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: 'It's not the rational way.' That's what you're trying to say, isn't it?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: We're not here to take risks, not to waste Silence's courage. We're just waiting for her at the end.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Ifrit...
She realizes that Ifrit is much taller than she was a few years ago, when she was rescued from the laboratory.
In the face of impending danger, there is no impatience or recklessness in her eyes, only courage and wisdom.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Let's go.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Alright!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: By the way, Saria, I saw a falling star when I got to Trimounts.

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: A star? You mean the object that fell on the Triton factory in District 13?

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: It was a star!

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: And Silence told me a story where all our differences disappear when the stars fall.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: You and Silence are gonna make up, right?

steps.name: Saria
steps.text: Yes... we will.

steps.name: Ifrit
steps.text: Great!
Will they?
Saria turns back to look at the familiar streets of Trimounts.
The path she is about to tread suddenly feels unfamiliar.
She has overcome many challenges. What lies before her is far from a crisis.
But, for the first time, she feels out of control.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: Holy hell, I'm freezing!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Look out, there's a car.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: That was a close shave! Can't even think clearly in this cold.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: I tell you, sir, this weather, it's all that tech company's doing.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: They use drones to spray chemicals that make our lungs freeze with every breath.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: They want to kidnap us, put our brains in jars, and turn us into nutrients for their artificial sun.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: Look up there in the sky—

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: Those stars ain't stars. They're cameras that the monsters sent up there to watch our every move. They even kidnapped our president, put his skin on, and locked all of Columbia under their control!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Here's a few bills... Find a warm place to spend the night.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: I don't need money, sir. I'm just waiting for dawn to break.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: Between the two of us, I'm organizing a protest against the Vice President and these tech companies. The people must wake up!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Take this too. All my money. You can have it.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: Wait, sir...

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I knew I would find you here.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Good morning, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: One more cup of tea and the sun should be up. Time for me to go to work on the other side.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Enough with the act, Parvis. When did you start working with Kristen?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You, Jara, Justin Jr., and Nasti. You fooled me into thinking that I had Kristen isolated, that I was just one step from success.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I became a laughing stock! My gamble, all my efforts, just another rung on the ladder for her to climb!

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Tea, Ferdinand?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You...

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Underhanded old goat?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Let me make one thing clear: I don't know where Kristen is. She doesn't trust me so much, and I'm not so interested in her secret.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But you didn't come to ask questions. Otherwise, you would have brought the muscle you borrowed from that colonel, as you did with Jara.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: It's not like you to swallow insults from Pioneers, and come back to grovel at the feet of the Colonel after he abandoned you once.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You set your mind to it. Why did you give up so close to the truth?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: No wild guesses.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Perhaps you should look at yourself in the mirror, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're jealous of her.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're jealous that she gets men to fight for her, even when she's not around.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're jealous that it only took her a few words to earn the loyalty that took you so much time and money to buy.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: You're jealous of her charisma.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: There's a part of you, somewhere deep down, that's enthralled by her. The more you deny it, the more you hate her—

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Why are you telling me this?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Because it's how I feel.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Look outside, Ferdinand.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: When I was little, I never saw stars in the night sky.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: All I saw was the silhouette of the great spire, the light of witchcraft lightning up the skies.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Adults told me it was the eye of the Witch King, watching over every inch of Leithanien.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: And I thought, what was the meaning of life, if the Witch King was the sole miracle chosen by fate?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Didn't you despise the efforts of those stupid casters who wanted to summon the Witch King's souls?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Yes, I opposed it.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: My kin and former colleagues spent their entire lives trying to recreate a fleeting miracle in this time and age.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But in my long years of research, I've realized that a miracle is so because it is a coincidence that cannot be controlled or recreated.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Only such a coincidence can break the cage of fate that traps us all.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You see Kristen as that coincidence?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: She has the potential to create miracles.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: You have your dream, and I have mine. If she is the fated miracle, than what are we? Waste coming off the production line? Meaningless noise?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Why despair, Ferdinand?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Perhaps the fate of mankind does hinge upon one singularity, who will break all shackles and become the eyes of all, to see sights that we could not have imagined.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: But that does not mean our lives are destined to fall by the wayside.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Miracles are born in the journey of evolution. A journey made up of all our dreams: Yours, mine, even that foolish tramp outside.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Why are you telling me this?

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: Feeling better? Have some tea. It'll put some color in your face, so you won't be so embarrassed when the kids see you on their way to work.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: I've lost everything. There isn't much for you to remember.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: I'm in no hurry. We can talk about work once you're done with your tea.

steps.name: Parvis
steps.text: It's always good to chat with an old friend. We took our first steps together, after all.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: Hello there, good sir!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Megaphone and sign boards?

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: This is what you spent the money on? Not food and blankets?

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: There are things more important than creature comforts!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Give me that board.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: 'Rhine Lab.' At least spell the company's name right if you're going to protest it.

steps.name: Homeless Resident
steps.text: That's much better! Thank you, sir!

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: Tell me.

steps.name: Ferdinand
steps.text: What do you dream of? What is the future you're fighting for?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: How do you like my vivarium, Doctor?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Nobody can just barge in. And Rosmontis seems to like it.
Rosmontis stands quietly in the verdant lab.
She carefully observes each plant, then meticulously records their form in her notebook.
Her gaze stops on the last page of the notebook.
You know it is where that letter is kept.

options: Are you still reading the letter, Rosmontis?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Yes, Doctor.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I want to remember what happened today and record it in my terminal, before I forget.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Loken... Loken Williams...

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: What is the 'home' that he talked about like? Is it like Rhodes Island?

options: No.
No way.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Then he's not my family.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I don't like him, Doctor. I came into contact with many feelings that I didn't like through him.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I want to pick them out and put them somewhere that won't bother me. Amiya helped me clean them up before she left, but they keep growing.

options: What kind of feelings?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: ...Loss.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: And... destruction.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I want to destroy them. It's not right. Pith would be angry...

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: I shouldn't see Loken again, should I, Doctor?

options: Do you want to learn about your past, Rosmontis?

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Memory is precious. I don't want to use it on bad things.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: But I want to see with my own eyes again. I want to know what I would do.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: It may not be to learn... it may be to throw it away again.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: But I'll say goodbye properly this time.

options: Okay.
We'll find Loken.
Get some rest before that, though.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Mm-hm...

options: (Give Rosmontis your jacket)
(Put your jacket on Rosmontis's shoulders)
Go to sleep.

steps.name: Rosmontis
steps.text: Mm... Doctor...
The young Feline lies down at your side, clutching the jacket you gave her tightly.
Her breathing is fragile yet resilient, as it is when she is awake.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: She's tired.

options: Rosmontis's Arts are heavily dependent on intention.
The day took a toll on her.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: What about you, Doctor?

options: Let's talk somewhere else, let Rosmontis sleep.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Your brow's furrowed.

options: Should I cooperate with the army's investigation?
Should I surrender to the Maylander Foundation?
Rhodes Island has been dragged into the maelstrom of Trimounts.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I arranged for you to go to Rhine. I have proof that you had legitimate reasons to enter the HQ building, and that you have nothing to do with the attack on the Vice President.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The army can't actually do anything about you. Don't worry about them.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Ho'olheyak just loves to drag people into these messes... kooky bint.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: There's no real witness to the 'crime scene,' though.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hard to say if the Maylander Foundation would really believe that some completely unrelated person lopped off the head of one of their top agents, or if they suspect that it's all just an act.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The explosion at the Triton factory, the attack on the Vice President, Kristen's disappearance... Trimounts is in chaos right now.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It may be irresponsible to say this, but neither the army nor the Maylander Foundation have time to deal with Rhodes Island. You're not at the center of the maelstrom.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: No need to be so nervous, Doctor.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Still, I'm responsible for your situation here. Our partnership's still good. You helped me, and I'll do my best to help you.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: If it comes to it, I can arrange to get you, Rosmontis, and Iffy out of Trimounts right now.

options: That's not what I'm concerned about, Muelsyse.
Sincerity is the foundation of cooperation, Muelsyse.
You're looking for both Saria and Kristen?
Are you trying to stop something, or to put something right?
Your position has been vague from the beginning.
We're partners, but I don't know what you really think.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: A dance, Doctor?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's no fun being interrogated like this.
Muelsyse puts her hands behind her back, turns around, and takes a couple of steps. She looks back at you with a rare, serious expression on her face.
Music fills the air.
It is a relaxed, soothing tune. You see moisture seep from the leaf veins, converging into a drop of dew.
More drops appear, leaving the leaves and catching up to you and Muelsyse, moving with the flow of the melody. You see the rhythm of each droplet, light as breath.
They are the melody itself.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Feel it, Doctor. It will guide our steps.

options: Your droplets seem 'free' in this vivarium.
The air in this vivarium seen 'clean'.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Very astute, Doctor.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: From lightning to irrigation to atmosphere control, none of the systems in this vivarium employ Originium technology. It is the cleanest place in Trimounts.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: This is the one place in Trimounts where I feel at ease.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oftentimes, I choose to operate through a clone not because I want to.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But because I have to.
Muelsyse disappears from your vision. You find your hand holding nothing but air.
The droplets form a ribbon of water, gently pulling you towards a corner of the vivarium.

steps.name: Automated Commentary
steps.text: The Pale Fir is extremely sensitive to its environment. Pollution from Originium industries have reduced its habitat to a small number of hilly areas in Columbia.
The droplets scatter and shatter, creating a mist between you and the firs.
You see the faint silhouette of a tombstone. Muelsyse sits quietly by it, picking away at the weeds that surround it.
You have never seen her so sad.
Is it a shadow of the past?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I grew up in an orphanage in Trenton, near Trimounts.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The headmaster said I was found on the doorsteps of the orphanage. No one knows who my parents are.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I realized at an early age that I was different.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: My powers are unique, but they are not Originium Arts. I'm much more sensitive to Originium than most people; even a slight increase in Originium concentration is enough to affect my health.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: What am I? No one knows.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That's why I've searched for the answer since I was little. Ironically, it's also the reason why my grades have always been good.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Finally, I found that word hidden away in some ancient books.

options: 'Elves.'

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: The word is not unknown to you... you do have many secrets, don't you, Doctor?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Well, it's not important.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Anyway, I tracked down my biological parents' old Trimounts home, but the house had long since changed hands.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I followed the trail they left behind, and eventually found where they went.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's this village right here... so remote I thought I made a mistake. Most of the buildings have fallen into ruin, they look to be centuries-old.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I didn't see anyone. I had a feeling as I went into the hills behind the village...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I saw a simple cemetery surrounded by pale firs, where dozens of tombstones lay.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: This village was not an Elven settlement. It was their graveyard.
Muelsyse stands up, looks at you, and fades away into the mist before the firs.
Your partner returns to your side.

options: Elven nature forced you to distance yourselves from modern civilization.
Why did your parents abandon you?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Distancing oneself from modern civilization is easier said than done.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: To spend your life in remote mountains, when you know that a more convenient, more advanced, more interesting life is right there, waiting for you to reach out.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: How are we, with our long lifespans, supposed to accept it?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Some of my people faded away in sorrow, some chose to end their own lives.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: More Elves chose to go into society, including my parents.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They lived cautiously but bravely, looking for ways to survive in civilization without coming into contact with Originium.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They knew Originium would kill them, someday. They accepted it.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They contracted Oripathy.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Elves are highly sensitive to Originium and lack resistance to Oripathy symptoms. Few live more than a month after contracting Oripathy.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Like most Elves, they could not accept spending the rest of their days in remote mountains, and sought a more convenient, more advanced, more interesting life, despite the dangers.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: They knew Originium would kill them, someday. They accepted it.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Knowing their days were numbered, they left me behind in a village far away from the cities, and returned to the place where they came from, to await the coming of death.

options: Do you find it regrettable? Or absurd?
Are you looking for a way to change the fate of your people?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Next dance, Doctor.
More droplets rise in the vivarium, as the music enters a new passage.
The smile returns to Muelsyse's face. The melody sings on. You do not know if the topic will continue.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Sometimes I envy Rhodes Island. There are so many people there.

options: You came to Rhodes Island.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Oh, you knew?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I sneaked in once or twice to see if Iffy was doing well, and see what Saria was doing.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And I saw someone standing on the deck, gazing at the sunset, lost in thought.

options: I didn't notice you.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Don't tell anyone. Just one of my tiny clones. No danger to anybody.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I thought, why would you be up on the deck with only your thoughts for company, when there's so much joy waiting down below?

options: I wanted to see if I could remember anything.
I feel like there used to be someone I would watch the sunset with.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Did you find any memories of that person?

options: No.
After all these years, all I know is a name.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: So there are answers beyond even your reach. That makes things seem a little bit fairer.
She leads you on, doing a half pirouette.

options: You're a good dancer.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Of course I am. I was the ace of my university dance team.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: After I left the village, I spent all my time studying.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Every Columbian child knows that science and tech are the best way to change your life.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I studied to become the top of my class, then went to school in Trimounts, where I stayed on top.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I spent a lot of effort to blend into modern life. Fashion, gaming, literature, music, dance... I studied etiquette, met a lot of people.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: For others, these are hobbies, but for me, it's a mission, an exploration, a test.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I know it sounds weird, but I tasked myself to live life as hard as I could.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It's been a long time since I danced, though.

options: With Saria and Kristen?

steps.text: The droplets go around you. The lights of the vivarium cannot penetrate them. They hold fragments of the past, gentle, clear, yet untouchable.
The newly renovated lab, mostly empty bottles... Saria, and Kristen? And Muelsyse, with a disappointed look on her face.
The three stare at each other in middle of the room, like three wooden mannequins.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: New Year's Eve, not long after Rhine Lab was founded... everyone was happy. I was the happiest.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I met Kristen and Saria shortly before I graduated.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Kristen is not your average investor's preferred partner. You know you're in for surprises the moment you see her, and not all of them are gonna be pleasant. As for Saria, she just felt steady as a rock.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: My advisor happened to be involved with a project of theirs, but she wasn't very interested, so she sent me in her stead.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I had nothing back then, other than my obsession with living hard. I tried everything and went nowhere. They helped me get over a period when I was lost between my identities as a graduating student and as an Elf.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: It was just me, Kristen, Saria, Parvis and Ferdinand at the time.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Parvis hid himself upstairs, saying he couldn't stay up all night. Ferdinand left early for other business.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Can you believe it? At the end of the day, I couldn't find anyone to dance with me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I ended up grabbing Saria... and Kristen.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: None of us knew how to dance in threes. I can still remember the looks on their faces!

options: Why are you so obsessed with Kristen?
Rhine Lab is important to you.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Because of my dream.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: We agreed she would help Nasti set out on her journey, and she'll bring my dream with her.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: ...To be more precise, Saria and Kristen are important to me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: I've always believed that we'll only get where we really want to be if the two of them work together.
The music ends. The vivarium is empty, except for Muelsyse standing opposite you, calm as a pale fir.
You hear the sound of the air circulation system running.
The wind on your face feels unusually moist. The scent of plants, the soft earth... you realize that the droplets of water, the music, and the dance really existed.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You've found my wobbliness, Doctor. Yes, I'm trying to manipulate everyone, including you...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: But everything I do, I do for myself, the few kin that I have left, so we can breathe, feel the wind, run, travel freely...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: To make our journey a little less hard.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: All I've done, I did to keep the few friends I have, so that in this city, I won't be so...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: This is all I can tell you. All I can promise you.

options: There are a lot of things you haven't made clear.
There are a lot of gaps in your story.
Should I trust you?
You didn't really manipulate me.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: And so...

options: Help me one more time, Muelsyse.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Hm?

options: I must find Loken Williams.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Even if I could help you... why do you not ask me to help you and Rosmontis get out of Trimounts safely?

options: We've come too far to turn back now.
Rhodes Island only goes forward.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Saria and Dr. Kal'tsit have reason to get involved. But what about you? Will you get to the bottom of all this, even if the price is a two-front war with the military and Maylander?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: That's not the most logical choice.

options: I want to help Rosmontis.
I want the truth.
I want to find myself.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: She's sleeping soundly...

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: You want to find her lost past?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Are you so interested in Kristen's dream?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Do you believe you'll find your past in Trimounts?

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Alright... we have a deal.

steps.name: Muelsyse
steps.text: Our partnership will go on.
Who was that on the phone?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: A lonely soul, searching for companions.
Since when have you two become such close friends?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: We just happened to be going the same way for a while.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Same for you. When are you going to leave my lab? The smell of alcohol affects the equipment.
That's so cold.
Thanks to you and that agent's improvisation, I have a dozen calls to make tonight just to keep you out of jail. Like hell am I doing this sober.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: You got what you wanted. Is Kristen's price not enough for a businessman like you?
Price? Are you reminding me how much I lost to this crazy plan?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Then you should have gone to Kazimierz.
Join the Chamber and play with the knights and speculators?
Yes, the plan has been lying in my terminal for years. I could make more money, and do so in a safer way.
But all those great projects... they're about a nation, an era.
I want to seize the opportunity before me, to see a future far beyond anyone's wildest dreams rise from my palms.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: Is that a dream? From a practical person like you?
Anyone can dream. Especially facing the fickle tides of fate.
You put it astutely. Going the same way.
Look at those scientists. For all the conflicts they went through, from friend to foe and from foe to friend, they all end up on the same path.

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: They all saw a part of themselves in the least likely of all futures.
What about you?

steps.name: Nasti
steps.text: A meaningless question. Why do you think I've tolerated your presence for so long?
That's why I like the 'going the same way' part. Even if it's only temporary.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Miss Nasti Lunorey.

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: If we still have our life and liberty after tomorrow—

steps.name: Justin Jr.
steps.text: Will you come with me to the highest point in Trimounts, and take a good look at the sky that hasn't changed for thousands of years?
